issue_context.title: Spurious error reporting in PEM handling
issue_context.body:
This worked fine in 1.1.1 and earlier. Emits errors (but still works) in current master.

A test file that has a CSR, CERT and PRIVATE KEY within it.

This works perfectly in prior OpenSSL versions as it explicitly picks out the object that it wants in each pass.

Now we get an error message ... it still keeps going - but we should not be seeing an error condition coming out for this.

> openssl pkcs12 -inkey foo.pem -in foo.pem -export -out foo.pfx 
> 40955B1EDE7F0000:error:1608010C:STORE routines:ossl_store_handle_load_result:unsupported:crypto/store/store_result.c:151:
> 40955B1EDE7F0000:error:1608010C:STORE routines:ossl_store_handle_load_result:unsupported:crypto/store/store_result.c:151:
> 40955B1EDE7F0000:error:1608010C:STORE routines:ossl_store_handle_load_result:unsupported:crypto/store/store_result.c:151:
comments: Note associated with this is that the documentation for the PEM handling functions don't note that you can have multiple different objects in a file and it will only pull out what is required. This has always been the OpenSSL behaviour and the user expectation - and it is a documentation error that this isn't actually written in specifically.

review_comments: Wont you end up with a floating ERR_set_mark(), if you dont call ERR_clear_last_mark() here?
